pr_body:
Fixes #31138
This show message like:
```
ERROR: to_int: Cannot represent 1111111111111111111 as int, provided value is too big.
   At: core/ustring.cpp:1778.
```
when found overflow or underflow.
pr_comments: Maybe the message should tell that it happens due to overflow? Or even simpler - that the number is too big.

I added info about too big/small value to error message.

It is a little strange that in core/math/expression.cpp, `num` variable from below, is never negative(minus sign is added later), so in this case, error message is not accurate.
![file](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41945903/63416778-5f559880-c400-11e9-9075-59d0e31da606.gif)


https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/51def4dab9d0e787c519aef914764a6140565d90/core/math/expression.cpp#L1149
Maybe change "as a long int" with "as a 64-bit integer" in the error messages? Also, I'm not sure that `int64_t`'s maximum value is `LONG_MAX`.

> Also, I'm not sure that `int64_t`'s maximum value is `LONG_MAX`.

Indeed, at least the guaranteed max for `INT_MAX` would be 16-bit and for `LONG_MAX` would be 32-bit. In practice I think it's twice that for each on x86_64, but that's still a bit unclear whether this bounds properly match the actual implementation we have on each platform.

http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/climits/

issue_context.title: Int64_t overflows in GDScriptTokenizerText::_advance
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.dev.custom_build 7126654ea

**OS/device including version:**
Ubuntu 18.04

**Issue description:**
![Screenshot_20190806_142017](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41945903/62539583-d19d7900-b855-11e9-8668-eb165f3a2777.png)
Max int_64t value 9,223,372,036,854,775,808
```
core/ustring.cpp:1801:12: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2152153523423251523 * 10 cannot be represented in type 'long'
SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior core/ustring.cpp:1801:12 in 
```
comments: I am new to this project so can you elaborate on the issue?

The problem mentioned is that those lines can trigger an integer overflow:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7126654eafc5a50a782bfbcdcfcb243807662eab/core/ustring.cpp#L1793-L1808

This would happen if a large enough number is written out in GDScript, without any error being reported.

This is a potential problem because it can hide errors from the user (numbers that large cannot be represented and after the overflow would become completely different numbers) and because it is undefined behaviour in C/C++ (depending on the compiler and platform).

review_comments: This should be `INT64_MAX` and `INT64_MIN` since this function returns `int64_t`.
